ABSTRACT
THEORETICAL INVESTIGATION OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN
PLACE ATTACHMENT AND WELL-BEING
Avcı Türkoğlu, Beste
Master of Science, City Planning in City and Regional Planning
Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Anlı Ataöv Demirkan
May 2023, 294 pages
Contemporary approaches to urban planning often ignore the transformative effects
of modernity, post-modernity, and globalization on cities and places. The desire for
planning practices to remain static, their inability to adapt to change, and,
fundamentally, their disregard for the experience of place, result in the loss of
meaningful places. In this context, this thesis presents a theoretical investigation of
the intricate relationship between place attachment and well-being, delving into the
multifaceted dimensions of human experience and the significance of the place. With
an emphasis on the concepts of place, this study unravels the issues that bind
individuals to their surroundings, exploring the similarities and differences between
place attachment and well-being processes.
The thesis employs an in-depth exploration of existing theories, studies, and
frameworks to unveil the nuanced interplay between place attachment and well-
being. By integrating diverse perspectives, the thesis identifies approximately 65
significant indicators and builds a theoretical framework that includes six categories
the sense of the self, needs, perceptive cognitional, affective emotional, behavioral,
and social. The findings highlight commonalities and differences. Both literatures
emphasize the importance of self-identity, perceptions, thoughts, memories,
behaviors, and emotions. The findings also highlight the significance of culture in
v

both place attachment and well-being, related to self-identity, social relations,
beliefs-norms, and sense of community.
By juxtaposing the theoretical framework with practical insights gained from the
exemplified focus group study that adopts the fuzzy cognitive mapping technique,
this thesis aims to provide a better understanding of place attachment and its possible
impacts on individuals’ well-being for practitioners, policymakers, and designers.
Keywords: Place, Experience, Place Attachment, Place Identity, Well-being,
vi

Günümüz şehir planlama ve kentsel tasarım yaklaşımları, şehirlerin ve yerlerin
modernite, post-modernite ve küreselleşmenin etkisiyle değişmekte olduğunu göz
ardı etmektedir. Planlama pratiklerinin statik kalma arzusu, değişime adapte
olamayışı ve en temelde de yer deneyimini göz ardı edişi, var olan anlamlı yerlerin
ruhunu yitirmesine neden olmaktadır. Bu kapsamda tez, yere deneyimini yer
bağlılığı ile iyi olma arasındaki karmaşık ilişkiyi teorik olarak inceleyerek
çözümlemeyi, böylelikle insan deneyiminin çok yönlü boyutlarına ve yerin önemine
derinlemesine inmeyi amaçlamıştır. Bu çalışma bireyleri çevrelerine bağlayan
nedensellikleri açığa çıkararak, yer bağlılığı ile iyi olma süreçleri arasındaki
benzerlikleri ve farklılıkları keşfetmektedir.
Bu tez, yer bağlılığı ile iyi olma arasındaki karmaşık ilişkiselliği keşfetmek için
mevcut teorileri, çalışmaları ve çerçeveleri derinlemesine incelemektedir. Farklı
bakış açılarını entegre ederek, yaklaşık 65 önemli gösterge tespit edilmiş olup bu
göstergeler ile benlik duygusu, ihtiyaçlar, algısal bilişsel, duygusal duygulanımsal,
davranışsal ve sosyal olmak üzere altı kategoriden oluşan bir teorik çerçeve inşa
edilmiştir. Bulgular, ortak noktaları ve farklılıkları vurgulamaktadır. Her iki literatür
de öz kimliğin, algıların, düşüncelerin, anıların, davranışların ve duyguların önemine
vurgu yapmaktadır. Bulgular ayrıca, yer bağlılığı ve iyi olma hali açısından öz
vii

kimlik, sosyal ilişkiler, inançlar/normlar ve topluluk duygusuyla sıklıkla
ilişkilendirilen kültür kavramının önemini vurgulamaktadır.
Teorik çerçeveyi, bulanık bilişsel haritalama tekniklerini benimseyen örnek odaklı
grup çalışmasından elde edilen pratik bilgilerle bir araya getiren bu tez, yer
bağlılığını ve iyi olma hali üzerindeki olası etkilerini uygulayıcılar, politika yapıcılar
ve tasarımcılar için daha anlaşılır hale getirmeyi amaçlamaktadır.

CHAPTER 1
1 INTRODUCTION
“The place is created by human beings for human purposes. Every row of trees or
houses originally existed as an idea, which was then made into a tangible reality. A
building, a park, or a street corner does not, however, remain a place simply
because it is a tangible reality and was originally designed as a place. To remain a
place, it has to be lived in. This is a platitude unless it is examined what ‘lived in’
means. To live in a place is to experience it, to be aware of it in the bones as well
as with the head. Place, at all scales from an armchair to the nation, is a construct
of experience; it is sustained not only by timber, concrete, and highways but also
by the quality of human awareness”
(Tuan, 1975)
1.1 Problem Background and Rationale of the Study
The contemporary urban planning approach ignores the global urban changes which
affect the characteristics of many places all around the world due to the modernity,
post-modernity and globalization. People’s everyday lives and places’ identities are
undergoing a fundamental change as a consequence of the mobility of people,
migrations, cultural diversity, and heterogeneity in urban places. The increase in
ethnic and cultural diversity in societies with the migration movements has led to the
emergence of heterogeneous societies and the weakening of place identities.
Architects, planners and other authorities, in neglecting the meanings of places that
have importance for individuals and groups, “increase the risk of destroying
authentic places and/or producing inauthentic places” (Relph, 1981 as cited in
Gustafson, 2001). Sameness has begun to dominate places’ uniqueness and people’s
1

way of doing things. The places are becoming similar to each other by getting smaller
in terms of being known, accessible, and visible to all people (Perkins, 2011).
“Losing the characteristics of familiar and meaningful places to its users impacts the
continuity of place attachment which may, in turn, cause identity crises for
individuals” (Buttimer, 1980; Hay, 1991; Ujang, 2012).
The deficiency begins from not understanding the idea of place and recognizing the
significance of the place for a human being. “Space and place, which are two
fundamental components of the lived world”, evoke familiar meanings and schemas
in our minds through our everyday experiences (Tuan, 1974). However, scientific
discussions put forth the distinction between these two concepts. To define the
distinction in a nutshell, a place is described as “a set of spaces transformed into a
meaningful location through peoples’ experiences and ideas” (Leonard, 2013).
“Space is abstract. It lacks content; it is broad, open, and empty, inviting the
imagination to fill it with substance and illusion; it is a possibility and beckoning the
future. Place, by contrast, is the past and the present, stability and achievement”
(Tuan, 1975: 164). While the space is the dimension that people live in, the place is
the setting that individuals experience with their senses and feel attached to it by
giving meanings. Any happening cannot occur without a reference to a particular
place. The place is everywhere, which is an integrated part of all existence. Every
act and occurrence take place somewhere (Norberg-Schulz, 1979). Life itself takes
place somewhere. “Space is transformed into place as it acquires definition and
meaning by the user of that space” (Tuan, 1975). When the meaning that is given by
people and their experiences have been removed from a place, only space remains.
Inevitably, decisions and interventions made on such an indispensable part of human
existence will have an impact on every individual. The main problem here is that
urban planning practices have a limited perspective on how places are perceived by
people through their experiences and on an understanding of the value constructed
upon given meanings by them.
The journey of place experience requires a process that includes three phases. The
process of experience begins through sensory modes, which are direct and passive,
2

followed by active and indirect modes. “These modes range from the more direct
and passive senses of smell, taste, and touch, to active visual perception and the
indirect mode of conceptualization” (Tuan, 1974:8). The sensory modes lead the
movements of the human body in his surroundings to experience the space physically
in a more active way. The senses direct the body's perception of external stimuli and
the mind's conceptualization of meaning. The accumulation of experience and
meaning affects the individual’s perception, values, ideas, attitudes, and behavior
patterns, and a relationship occurs between the person and place. “Space has been
seen in distinction to place as a realm without meaning - as a 'fact of life' which, like
time, produces the basic coordinates for human life. When humans invest meaning
in a portion of space and then become attached to it in some way, it becomes a place”
(Cresswell, 2004:10).
The literature review declares that the established bond between people and place is
called as place attachment “which can vary through spatial level, degree of
specificity, and social or physical features of the place” (Scannell & Gifford, 2010).
Place attachment is “a bond manifested through affective, cognitive, and behavioral
psychological processes” (Lewicka, 2011), and can include feelings of involvement,
identification, and sense of belonging (Manzo, 2005). Place attachment is a
multifaceted concept that is influenced by a variety of individual and environmental
factors, including variables related to sense of the self, psychological and
physiological need, and social experiences as well as affective, cognitive, and
behavioral processes. The concept of place attachment has been mostly mentioned
together with the place identity. Place identity, on the other hand, refers to “the ways
in which an individual's self-concept is influenced by and reflects the place in which
they live” (Proshansky et al., 1983). These two concepts are often closely related, as
an individual's place attachment can influence their sense of place identity, and vice
versa (Stedman, 2002). Research has consistently demonstrated a positive
relationship between place attachment and place identity. For example, individuals
with strong place attachment tend to have a strong sense of place identity and a
greater identification with their community (Stedman, 2002). Place attachment and
3

place identity can also influence each other, as a strong sense of place identity can
lead to a stronger emotional attachment to a particular place (Ujang, 2012).
Jorgensen and Stedman (2002) state that “sense of place encompasses the sub-
concepts of place identity, place attachment, and place dependence”. As another
point of view, some of the researchers consider place attachment as the component
of place identity (Proshansky et al.,1983; Paasi, 1991; Lalli, 1992), while others
consider it vice versa (Altman and Low, 1992; Hummon, 1992), or as they are
synonyms (Brown and Werner, 1985; Antonsich, 2010).
Place attachment and place identity have been studied at various urban scales,
including home, neighborhood and city scales, and research has consistently found
that these concepts are related to individuals' sense of belonging and connection to
their physical environment. Hernández et al. (2007) argued that “place attachment
and place identity studies are mostly restricted to neighborhood scale and intensity
of attachment and identity are affected by size of the place”. Similarly, Lewicka
(2011) agrees with Hernández et al. (2007) by also highlighting that there are other
scales, including non-residential areas such as tourism centers, parks, recreation
areas, or public buildings which are explored in terms of place attachment and place
identity studies.
The literature also reveals that the psychological processes of place attachment
overlap with phases for achieving the well-being state (Harris, Werner, Brown, &
Ingebritsen, 1995; Arefi, 1999; Brown et al. 2003; Fresque-Baxter & Armitage,
2012; Ujang & Zakariya, 2014; Scannell & Gifford, 2017). Well-being refers to an
individual's overall sense of satisfaction and happiness in life. It is a multifaceted
concept that includes various components, such as positive emotions, personal
growth, and a sense of purpose. According to Ryff (1989), psychological well-being
is consisted of six elements: “self-acceptance, positive relations with others,
autonomy, environmental mastery, personal growth, and purpose in life”. These
dimensions are interrelated and contribute to an one’s sense of well-being. Other
researchers have identified additional factors that contribute to psychological well-
being. For example, Diener and Seligman (2002) proposed the concept of
4

“flourishing,” which involves experiencing positive emotions, engagement with
activities, positive relationships, meaning and purpose in life, and accomplishment.
In addition to individual factors, environmental factors, such as social support and
access to resources, can also influence psychological well-being (Keyes, 2005). For
example, individuals who have strong social support networks tend to have higher
levels of well-being (Sarason et al, 1990). Overall, psychological well-being is a
complex concept that is influenced by a variety of elements, including “individual
characteristics, environmental factors, the presence of positive emotions, personal
growth, and a sense of purpose”.
1.2 Aim and Scope
The research basically aims to enlighten the relationship between place attachment
and well-being. The theoretical framework is established through a review of the
existing literature on place attachment, place identity, and well-being. The
exemplified focus group study is designed to develop and expand upon this
framework.
The thesis aims to investigate the relationality between place attachment and well-
being. The contemporary urban planning approach, which is dominated by the threat
of becoming same and often disregards the importance of the meanings of places for
individuals and groups, increases the risk of destroying places meaningful for people
and producing places that are repetitive and dull. This rises the significance of
understanding the idea of place and recognizing the meaning of the place for a human
being. As the meaning is assigned to the place, a bond between people and place
establishes. The thesis also suggests that the processes of attachment to a place and
reaching a state of well-being have overlapping issues. So, it means that any form of
attachment to a place might have impacts on well-being states of people. The thesis
emphasizes the need to understand the idea of place and its relation to the human
experience through place attachment and its possible impacts on well-being.
5
